facts.statement: The genus Borealosuchus was named by Christopher Brochu in 1997 to reclassify several species previously assigned to the genus Leidyosuchus.
facts.quote: It was named by Christopher Brochu in 1997 for several species that had been assigned to Leidyosuchus.

facts.statement: Borealosuchus was a mid-sized crocodyliform, with the species B. wilsoni reaching approximately 3.2 to 4.5 meters in length.
facts.quote: Borealosuchus was a mid-sized crocodyliform, with B. wilsoni measuring approximately 3.2 - 4.5 m long.

facts.statement: The species B. acutidentatus has been estimated to have reached nearly 7 meters (23 feet) in length.
facts.quote: B.acutidentatus has been estimated at nearly 7 metres (23 ft) long.

facts.statement: The species B. formidabilis is particularly well-known due to the discovery of remains from many individuals at the Wannagan Creek site in North Dakota.
facts.quote: B. formidabilis is particularly well-known, represented by the remains of many individuals from the Wannagan Creek site in North Dakota.

facts.statement: While earlier studies suggested Borealosuchus belonged to Crocodylia, recent research classifies it as a basal eusuchian that does not belong to Crocodylia.
facts.quote: Although some earlier phylogenetic studies proposed Borealosuchus to be a member of Crocodylia, recent studies are now recovering Borealosuchus as a basal eusuchian not belonging to Crocodylia

facts.statement: The specific name of the species B. threeensis references Exit 3 of the New Jersey Turnpike, which is the closest highway exit to its type locality.
facts.quote: The specific name is a reference to Exit 3 of the New Jersey Turnpike, which is the closest highway exit to the type locality.

facts.statement: Borealosuchus fossils date from the Campanian to Priabonian stages, spanning from 83.6 to 33.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Priabonian (83.6 to 33.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: A sixth species, B. threeensis, was formally named in 2012.
facts.quote: A sixth species of Borealosuchus, B. threeensis, was named in 2012.

facts.statement: Fossils of the species B. threeensis were found in the Inversand Company Marl Pit in Gloucester County, New Jersey.
facts.quote: Fossils of this species were found in the Inversand Company Marl Pit of Gloucester County, New Jersey.

rejected.statement: Borealosuchus, meaning "northern crocodile", is an extinct genus of crocodyliforms that lived in North America from the Late Cretaceous to the Eocene.
rejected.quote: Borealosuchus (meaning "northern crocodile") is an extinct genus of crocodyliforms that lived from the Late Cretaceous to the Eocene in North America.
